title: Shortest Program for the Universe: Algorithmic Information Theory, Kolmogorov Complexity, and Solomonoff Universal Induction on Trial — From Hume's problem of induction & Shannon ensemble entropy to Solomonoff's 1964 2^-|p| universal Bayesian prior & Kolmogorov's 1968 individual-string complexity K(x); Cilibrasi & Vitanyi's parameter-free Normalized Compression Distance, Veness-Hutter-Silver's Monte-Carlo AIXI-CTW agent & Liu-Pass's FOCS 2020 equivalence between time-bounded K^t and cryptographic one-way functions vs. Chaitin's halting probability Omega & reference-machine constants, Wolpert's No-Free-Lunch theorem, and Bennett's Logical Depth

teenKit.tldr: We know a repeating pattern is simpler than random static, but classical statistics says they are equally likely. Algorithmic Information Theory fixes this by measuring data by the length of the shortest computer program needed to generate it.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This exact mathematical framework explains how modern AI compression works, why Occam's Razor actually holds up in physics, and how we tell deep biological structure apart from random noise.
keyTakeaways: Shannon information theory treats a repeating string and random coin flips as equally probable, exposing a massive blind spot for pattern recognition.
Kolmogorov complexity measures the information content of an object by finding the length of the absolute shortest computer program that can output it.
Solomonoff Induction mathematically proves that simpler explanations are overwhelmingly more likely to predict the future correctly in any computable universe.

vocab.meaning: The length of the shortest computer program that can generate a specific piece of data, acting as the ultimate mathematical measure of its true complexity.
A mathematical formula giving a higher probability to shorter computer programs, turning William of Ockham's medieval philosophy into an exact law of probability.
A parameter-free trick using file compressors to measure how similar two files are, successfully used to reconstruct evolutionary family trees of mammals without touching DNA.

A metric created by Charles Bennett that measures how much computational time is required to unpack a piece of data, separating trivial random noise from deeply structured things like living organisms.

quiz.question: According to classical Shannon probability, how do a 1-million-bit repeating '01' string and a 1-million-bit string of pure random coin flips compare?
options: The repeating string is much more probable.
The random string is much more probable.
They have the exact identical probability of occurring.
Neither string can be measured by classical probability.
quiz.explanation: Classical probability treats any specific sequence of 1 million coin flips as equally rare, assigning them both a probability of two to the negative one-millionth power.

quiz.question: What does Kolmogorov complexity use as its fundamental unit of measurement to define the complexity of an individual string?
options: The length of the shortest computer program that can generate it
The total amount of physical energy required to compute it
The number of times the string appears in a standard text file
The elapsed time it takes a human to read the string aloud
quiz.explanation: Kolmogorov complexity defines the information content of any object precisely by the length of the shortest code or algorithm needed to produce it.

quiz.question: Why does David Wolpert's No-Free-Lunch Theorem argue that Occam's Razor (preferring simpler explanations) works in our universe?
options: Because simple explanations are inherently more magical than complex ones.
Because our physical reality just happens to be a low-complexity universe where simple patterns dominate.
Because human brains are physically too small to understand complex equations.
Because computers cannot process information without a built-in bias.
quiz.explanation: Wolpert proved that universal algorithms perform equally well across all possible universes averaged together, meaning Occam's Razor only works because our specific universe is fundamentally compressible.
